description: I am a college student passionate about web development and technology. I enjoy creating user-friendly websites using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. For the Earth Information Jukebox challenge, I aim to build an interactive Earth science platform. I am looking for creative teammates skilled in web development, UI/UX design, research, and data visualization.
summary:
The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive, retro-futuristic web application that transforms 45 years of NASA Earth science data and satellite visualizations into synchronized real-time music. Inspired by a spinning vinyl turntable, the app maps live NASA POWER climate telemetry (surface temperature, precipitation, and solar irradiance) and NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) / Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) frames into harmonious Web Audio (Tone.js) soundscapes across a 4-channel DJ stem mixer.

To address the challenge of making complex climate data accessible and engaging, users can click any coordinate on our interactive NASA GIBS satellite map, compare decades with a 1985 vs. 2025 A/B Time Machine, generate a personalized Climate Lifetime Soundtrack, or activate an Eyes-Closed Museum Audio Guide with stereo temporal panning and spoken milestone narration.

This project is important because it breaks down visual barriers for blind and low-vision communities while turning abstract planetary vital signs into an emotional, intuitive experience anyone can hear and understand.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive single-page web application that transforms 45 years (1981–2025) of NASA Earth science telemetry and satellite imagery into real-time generative music synchronized with visual timelines.

  • Live Satellite & Climate Data Pipeline: Users can choose from 12 curated planetary "records" (including global composite anomalies, Western Ghats monsoons, Arctic sea-ice retreat, Amazon droughts, and 8 NASA Earth Information Center / Scientific Visualization Studio datasets) or click anywhere on an interactive Leaflet.js map layered with NASA GIBS WMTS satellite tiles (MODIS_Terra_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor and AIRS_L2_Surface_Air_Temperature_Day). Clicking any coordinate queries the NASA POWER REST API for monthly surface temperature (T2M), precipitation (PRECTOTCORR), and solar irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN), calculating anomalies against a 1981–2010 GISTEMP baseline normal (with an automatic physical climate model fallback for offline resilience).
    1. Surface Temperature (T2M) → Analog Synth Lead: Rising temperatures glide to higher pitches and open a low-pass filter (400 Hz–4,200 Hz).
    2. Precipitation (PRECTOTCORR) → Acoustic Marimba Arpeggio: Rainfall rate scales note trigger density and stereo ping-pong delay shimmer.
    3. Solar Irradiance (ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN) → Lush Cosmic Pad: Modulates harmonic chord richness and atmospheric swell.
    4. Extreme Climate Anomaly → Crystal Bell Chime: Triggers an audible chime whenever warming exceeds $+1.35^\circ\text{C}$ above baseline or extreme rainfall occurs.
  • EIC SVS Visual Studio & Pixel-to-Sound Mode: Implements the NASA SVS Caldwell 73 (SVS 13786) framework via an animated radar scanline and pixel-sampling engine that maps vertical spatial coordinates to pitch, pixel luminosity to volume, and RGB color channels to distinct instrument timbres.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Inclusive Access for Blind & Low-Vision Audiences: Traditional climate dashboards rely heavily on visual charts. Our Eyes-Closed Museum Audio Guide uses Tone.Panner stereo spatialization (panning historical 1980s decades to the left ear and modern 2020s decades to the right ear) alongside window.speechSynthesis narration announcing milestone climate events, paired with full keyboard navigation and WCAG AAA contrast.
  • Emotional & Personal Climate Literacy: By translating abstract numbers into visceral sound—through a 1985 vs. 2025 A/B Time Machine that plays back-to-back decade loops and a Your Climate Lifetime Soundtrack builder keyed to the user's birth year—students, educators, and the public can immediately hear how Earth has warmed within their own lifetime.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3 (Glassmorphism UI, custom CSS variables, responsive grid), and Vanilla ES6+ JavaScript (bundle.js zero-build architecture for instant static deployment).
  • Audio & Visualization Libraries: Tone.js (v14.8.49) & native Web Audio API (DSP synths, filters, reverb, stereo panning, FFT waveform analysis), Chart.js (v4.4.1) (dual-axis synced timeline with custom vertical playhead plugin), Leaflet.js (v1.9.4), and HTML5 Canvas (60fps spinning Earth-vinyl turntable and SVS radar visualizer).
  • NASA Data & Services: NASA POWER API, NASA EOSDIS GIBS WMTS, NASA GISTEMP v4 baselines, and the NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) / Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) Content Database.
  • Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages ([https://gerald24rr059.github.io/Alpha-Orionis/](https://gerald24rr059.github.io/Alpha-Orionis/)).

Creativity & Design Considerations

  • Tactile Retro-Futuristic Jukebox Metaphor: Rather than presenting a sterile scientific dashboard, we designed an interactive Spinning Earth-Vinyl Turntable with concentric audio-reactive data rings, an animated mechanical tonearm, RPM tempo switches (1x/2x/4x), vinyl scratch interaction, and a live "What You Are Hearing" Decoder Pill that translates active musical stems into plain English in real time.
  • Reliability, Zero-Friction UX & Compliance: We engineered a zero-backend static bundle that works offline or online without CORS bottlenecks, added a 3-step dismissible onboarding banner so judges can start listening within seconds, and included explicit NASA non-endorsement notices and dataset citations throughout the interface.
